description: Execution-level technical evidence (stroke direction, tool behavior, pentimenti, corrections) for the Florentine Codex.
status: Merged: seed sample + field notebook transcriptions (all three FC volumes), 2026-06-22.

entries.note_text: Four figures on woven thrones face each other; a lead-point practice drawing of the upper-left figure's throne appears in the lower-left margin, connected by a lead-point line to the finished illustration -- likely a compositional aid for rendering three-dimensional form.

European (oak-gall type) ink has degraded the paper support; the capital letter beneath the illustration is separating from the paper in its lower-left section, an effect partially visible even in the Giunta facsimile.

Lead-point glosses naming kings appear above associated illustrations in the section on rulers; e.g. 'motecucoma' written above the king identifiable by an associated glyph, with a small lead-point sketch of the glyph itself adjacent.
Execution-by-stoning scene: a previous arm position (raised, stone held behind the head) covered with white paint; uncovered lead-point lines to the left of the body indicate the temporary position.
Sacrifice scene: flames originally drawn coming from the victim's chest cavity have been painted over.

Column of burning stones illustration: a drawn line of smoke perpendicular to the column has been painted over; lead-point drawing of stones to the left of the column visible both as physical indentation and as covered with white paint. Lead-point drawing also visible to the lower left of the figure group.
entries.essay_reference: 2008-09 comparative essay, Fig. 19 / field notebook gridded tracing

entries.note_text: Twelve textual corrections visible only on the original, not the facsimile; errors covered in white paint and corrected with a wide-nibbed writing tool. Corrections cluster around insertion of 'ch' (e.g. qui in mochoquiz, pachotinemi, tealtranime), suggesting a revised orthographic convention for representing Nahuatl sounds.

Cut-out illustration (approx. 5.5 x 4.5 cm) pasted over an earlier, unfinished version of the same scene (a group of women, no tears drawn, black line only, no color). The only known instance of this correction type in the Florentine Codex.
Split-nib pen evidence (likely native reed pen) in fine illustration work: lines within the dragonfly (375R), tiles (374V), flowers and garment folds (373R). Too fine to reproduce in facsimile.
Tracing of figure with marotte/staff-like diagonal element inside circular frame; short glyph-like text traced below the illustration.
Minimal hatching, non-evident dry media except in lower illustration; split-nib evidence in shading on the left leg of the Xipe Totec figure.

Eagle-catching-bird composition entirely redrawn across this opening; earlier eagle and bird, nest, and cliff face whited out and repositioned; standing eagle on 200R initially drawn covering a flying eagle beneath, later whited out and recolored.
After 'el septingessimo octavo' a line is scratched out. Reads: 'El septingessimo nono edificiero, se llamanos'.

Capital P visible burning through from recto. Heavy wear on lower right corners of rectos from ff. 1–48, diminishing after. Laid paper lines clearly visible from contrast built up by years of handling.
Huitzilopochtli and [Tezcatlipoca?] have offset their lines within the first inch of the spine.
uncertain_readings: Second deity name reads 'Tezcapoyal' or 'Tezcatlipoca' in notebook

entries.note_text: Stem of Quetzalcoatl and black sun and center dot of Tezcatlipoca [?] offset across the opening.
Latin phrase noted in margin. Reads approximately 'Caput de quorum(?) q[uartom]?'.
uncertain_readings: Latin phrase nearly illegible; 'quorum' and 'quartom' both uncertain
